name: Argument prioritization, grouping, and organization
definition: Lead with the strongest points, group claims to emphasize common issues, and present concise, non‑repetitive, well‑organized arguments in responses/briefs.

name: Drawing clarity, legibility, and sufficiency
definition: Provide figures that are clear and readable (appropriate line weights, no clutter) and that sufficiently depict the invention’s embodiments to aid understanding and claim support without adding unintended limits.

name: Evidentiary support and sufficiency
definition: Submissions present all relevant facts and are substantiated with citations, reasoning, declarations, and timely evidence; avoid conclusory assertions.

name: Plain‑language drafting and audience fit
definition: Use simple, precise language tailored to intelligent non‑experts and experts; avoid unnecessary jargon and define terms so the text is easy to follow, especially in claims.

name: Robust, well‑supported disclosure
definition: Provide detailed, enabling technical disclosure with multiple embodiments, alternatives, examples, and supportive drawings to fully support present and future claim scope.

name: Terminology management and consistency
definition: Ensure defined terms (especially specialized ones) are introduced and expressly defined, and are used consistently across the claims, specification, and filings to avoid shifting meaning.

name: Utility requirement — practical use
definition: The invention demonstrates a specific, credible, practical use.
